scope: One inflected verbal derivative. Reviewed sanadi chains, then Satf/tfc/ktavatu, then nominal gender/case/number. Classical formal derivation; not a claim that every generated long form is textually attested.

licensing.Satf: 3.2.124 licenses present active participles in suitable non-nominative agreement. Pilot restricted to cases2–7, not nominative or vocative.
licensing.tfc: 3.1.133 licenses agent nouns from verbal roots. Pilot specifies agent meaning.
licensing.ktavatu: 3.2.102 licenses the past active participle, referring to the agent.
licensing.derived_stems: 3.1.32 supplies dhatu status after sanadi; previously reviewed construction chains reused. Direct san+san remains excluded.

limits: Six reference checks support selected formation and declension rules; they do not independently certify all320 task keys.
Primary nominative examples test the engine against grammar citations; they are not used as paid Satf tasks.
Inspect systematic model disagreements and alternative spellings before release.
No arbitrary kvasu, feminine aka derivatives, Vedic forms or Curadi in this pilot.
hypothesis: Interactions between derived stems, participial num suppression, suffix-specific stem changes and nominal endings may yield new one-form difficulty. This is a hypothesis, not a threshold guarantee.
